topic: Bernard Baars (1988-2005): Global Workspace Theory — How a Single Conscious 'Stage' Broadcasts to Billions of Unconscious Specialists
visual_mode_reason: Baars's theater metaphor (one narrow spotlighted stage broadcasting simultaneously to dark auditorium rows of specialized processors) maps 1:1 onto long-range frontoparietal cortical broadcast versus local unconscious sensory modules.

primary_case.title: Bernard J. Baars's contrastive analysis of conscious vs unconscious processing ('Global Workspace Theory')
primary_case.place: Wright Institute / Neurosciences Institute, San Diego, California

people.name: Bernard J. Baars
people.role: Cognitive neurobiologist who solved the paradox of why consciousness is tiny and serial while the unconscious brain is vast and parallel

people.name: Herbert Simon & Allen Newell

core_facts.fact: First formulated in his 1988 book A Cognitive Theory of Consciousness and synthesized neurobiologically in Progress in Brain Research (2005), Bernard Baars tackled a central riddle: why can an 86-billion-neuron supercomputer consciously hold ONLY ONE conversation or ambiguous image at a time?

Baars used 'contrastive analysis' — comparing tight experimental pairs where nearly identical inputs stay unconscious vs cross into consciousness (e.g., binocular rivalry, masked words, unattended dichotic speech, automatic vs novel skills).

Unconscious brain networks (grammar parsing, balance, retinal edge detection, heart regulation) are VAST, fast, parallel, and isolated — each specialist module does its job quickly without knowing what distant modules are doing.
Conscious awareness, by contrast, is NARROW (~1 scene, 1 inner voice), serial, and slightly slower — yet buys one superpower no isolated module possesses: GLOBAL BROADCASTING.

Like an actor stepping into a bright spot on a theater stage in front of a dark auditorium of thousands of silent experts, the instant ONE piece of information wins entry to the Global Workspace, it broadcasts simultaneously to memory, language, motor planning, and emotion.

Consider binocular rivalry: show a house to the left eye and a face to the right eye simultaneously — both retinas and primary visual cortices fire continuously, yet you consciously see ONLY the face OR ONLY the house at any moment, broadcasting whichever wins across frontoparietal cortex.

Crucially, Baars warned against the 'Cartesian Theater' fallacy (Dennett): there is NO tiny little person sitting inside your head watching the stage — the 'audience' IS the distributed network of unconscious cortical/subcortical specialist circuits receiving the broadcast.

Recent multi-lab adversarial tests (Cogitate Consortium 2023-2025) put Global Workspace Theory head-to-head against Integrated Information Theory, confirming widespread cortical broadcast on task-relevant ignition while actively debating exact prefrontal vs posterior timing.

wow_facts.fact: Your unconscious brain processes millions of sensory bits in parallel every second — yet your conscious mind can't even listen to two simple sentences at the exact same moment. Why? Because consciousness isn't the worker — it's the PA loudspeaker.
wow_facts.why_surprising: Only one voice can use a building-wide loudspeaker at a time without turning into static.

wow_facts.fact: Feed a picture of a house into your left eye and a face into your right eye at the exact same instant: both eyes keep firing nonstop, yet your conscious world flips cleanly from 100% Face to 100% House every few seconds.
wow_facts.why_surprising: One winner takes the whole global broadcast stage.

wow_facts.fact: Ever had a name stuck 'on the tip of your tongue'? Your conscious stage is empty — just broadcasting a silent 'WANTED' poster out to dark auditorium rows until five minutes later an unconscious memory specialist shouts 'Archimedes!' onto the stage.
wow_facts.why_surprising: Global broadcast lets you recruit specialist modules you don't even know how to search.

wow_facts.fact: There is NO 'little viewer' sitting in the balcony of Baars's theater — the audience IS your motor, language, and memory networks listening in.
wow_facts.why_surprising: That single insight avoids the infinite homunculus trap.

misconceptions.myth: Consciousness does all the heavy computational lifting in your brain while the unconscious is primitive.
misconceptions.truth: Unconscious specialist circuits handle stunningly complex syntax, vision, and motor math; consciousness provides flexible cross-brain integration when routines hit novelty.

misconceptions.myth: Global Workspace Theory claims there is a literal 'screen' watched by a mini-self in the frontal lobe.
misconceptions.truth: Baars explicitly modeled AI 'blackboard architectures': global availability TO specialist modules IS conscious access, with zero inner spectator.

misconceptions.myth: You can consciously multitask two verbal streams simultaneously with zero loss.
misconceptions.truth: Because the Global Workspace is serial (~one broadcast coalition at a time), 'multitasking' two conversations is actually rapid, costly stage-switching.

misconceptions.myth: Science has 100% settled every neural detail of consciousness.
misconceptions.truth: Global Workspace remains a leading testable contender actively refined through adversarial trials against posterior-cortex and integrated-information rivals.

everyday_hooks: Forgetting a movie actor's name at dinner, broadcasting the mental question once, talking about dessert, and having the name pop onto your conscious stage ten minutes later.

Learning to drive stick-shift (hogging 100% of your conscious stage) versus driving years later on unconscious specialist autopilot until sudden black ice pulls driving straight back onto the global stage.
Trying to read a text while listening to a podcast — and realizing one stream went completely blank the instant the other took the microphone.
Writing a tricky problem clearly on a whiteboard ('external workspace') before sleep so unconscious specialists work on it.
